name: Fullscreen
plain: Takes over the whole screen for a page element after a click.
meaning: A site can hide the browser UI, which helps video and games but also lets a malicious page draw a fake desktop or browser bar. Esc always exits.

access.prompt_ui: No prompt (needs a click, tap or keypress)
access.persistence: Ends on Esc, navigation or exitFullscreen(); no stored state
access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Cross-origin iframe needs allow="fullscreen" (Permissions Policy fullscreen defaults to self)
steps: Page calls requestFullscreen within about 5 s
Browser shows Press Esc to exit message

limits.headline: Can make a video or page area fill your screen, after you tap
limits.user_action: You tap a Full screen button, or press a key like F on a video.
can: Fill the screen with a video, a game or a photo after a tap or key press
Hide the browser's toolbars while it is on
Stay full screen until you press Esc or swipe out
cannot: Go full screen without a tap, click or key press
Block the Esc key or the swipe that gets you out
Take over the whole iPhone screen for anything other than video
Hide that you are in full screen; browsers show a short banner
limits.differs: iPhone Safari is limited: video can go full screen, but most other page elements cannot. Android Chrome and desktop browsers allow it for any element.

story.what_it_is: After you click, a site can make part of the page fill your whole screen.

marketing.name: Fullscreen API
marketing.pitch: MDN says the API lets a site present an element, like a video or game, filling the whole screen.

story.for_you: You tap a full screen button on a video or game. The page fills your display and a small note tells you how to leave with Escape.
story.for_makers: Makers use it for immersion: video, games and slides. The click rule exists so a site cannot suddenly cover your screen with a fake desktop.

use_cases.example: You hit full screen on a movie and the player hides all the browser controls.
Xbox Cloud Gaming or GeForce NOW in the browser go full screen so it feels like a console.
A presenter shows slides full screen in a web deck.
A live sports stream fills your screen for the match.
A phishing page fakes a full screen browser window to steal passwords, which is why browsers show a warning.
A student opens a full screen exam page that locks out distractions.

technical_bounds: Needs transient user activation; promise rejects with TypeError otherwise
Esc (or system gesture) always exits; with Keyboard Lock the person must hold Esc for about 2 s
Browser shows an exit notice for a few seconds; Safari desktop limits some keys in fullscreen
iPhone Safari supports only video fullscreen through the native player (requestFullscreen on elements is iPad only)
Cannot enter fullscreen without a gesture even when previously allowed; the F11 user fullscreen is separate
Password and sensitive prompts from the OS or browser still render above

abuse: Fake OS or browser UI (fullscreen spoofing)

history.change: Unprefixed requestFullscreen that returns a promise
Standard Fullscreen API on iPad (iPhone still video only)
